camera: Straight top-down (bird's-eye) view, ship's nose pointing up toward the top of the frame, centered and filling most of the frame.
style: Detailed 16-bit-era pixel art, in the style of classic top-down shoot-'em-up sprites (Ikaruga, Raiden). Crisp hard-edged shapes, no soft gradients or airbrushed shading — use simple banded/dithered shading for depth instead. Limited, deliberate color palette (roughly 8-16 colors per ship). Strong, clean, iconic silhouette that reads instantly even at small size.
palette: Exact colors vary per ship/faction — always specified in the asset description below, not fixed here. Keep each faction's colors saturated and high-contrast against the dark background.
background: NO BACKGROUND AT ALL. Fully transparent behind and around the ship — the sprite is dropped straight onto the playfield, which the game draws itself in the sector's own colours. No tile, no panel, no card, no radial gradient, no vignette, no glow halo, no drop shadow: nothing but the ship, cut out to its silhouette.
constraints: Square 1:1 composition. No text, no logos, no watermarks, no UI elements, no drop shadow outside the subject.
_backgroundNote: This asked for a radial gradient from dark navy (#2f3b52) to near-black, and every sprite generated through generate-game-asset.yml duly baked one in — eighteen of the game's fifty-three icons, ten of them ships that draw on the board, each one a picture of a ship sitting on a dark tile sitting on a hex. A sprite carries no background. The dark field behind the fleet is the BOARD, and the renderer owns it.
wreckRule: A WRECK is a DERELICT — the same ship, dead in the water, NOT blown apart. Draw the SAME silhouette, the same hull plating and the same faction colours as that ship's own live icon, so the class is still recognisable at hex size: a Hauler's wreck is a dead Hauler. THE HULL STAYS IN ONE PIECE. No fragments, no confetti, no debris field, no detached chunks floating around it, nothing scattered off the silhouette: something has to be left that a salvage crew could cut open, a tug could tow, and an engineer could restart, and none of those are possible with a cloud of splinters. It must read as ONE object at 40 pixels across. Show it as disabled instead: scorch marks and blast scoring across the plating, one or two hull panels buckled, torn back or hanging loose but still attached, a crack or a punched hole or two with dark interior showing through, a bent antenna or a drooping gun barrel, and everything dead — no engine glow, no lit windows, no running lights, nothing emissive anywhere. No fire, no smoke, no explosion, no sparks: this is a cold hulk adrift, not the moment it died. Draw it at the LIVE ship's own colour and saturation — the renderer greys a wreck down itself (drawWreck in app.js), so a pre-greyed sprite comes out twice-dimmed. Same camera and same frame as the live sprite.
_wreckNote: Twenty-two of these, one per hostile class, generated separately through generate-game-asset.yml the same way the live icons were. Separate generations drift, and the answer here is this rule plus lockedPalette rather than a sheet: a sheet is for ANIMATION frames of one subject, where drift between frames is visible side by side in motion. These never appear together, and each has to match its own live sprite rather than the other twenty-one. INTACT IS THE LOAD-BEARING WORD. The first pass asked for pieces snapped off and drifting clear and got ships shattered into confetti, which no Tender could plausibly restart, no Collector could tow and nothing could cut open — three mechanics all resting on a wreck still being a ship. It was also unreadable at hex size, against the rule in this very entry. The one global transform — everything knocked toward grey so a wreck cannot read as a live ship — is done in the renderer instead of asked for here, because the first pass ignored it and came back as saturated as the live hull. Generate what the model draws well, construct the rest.
